title: Basic user-id as identity beside an encoded credential
summary: A synthetic log line that records the user-id in cleartext next to the Authorization header whose encoded token carries the same user-id and the password.
rationale: The password is the confidential portion; the user-id identifies the user but the scheme does not say whether it is public. Credential scope and personal-data scope are different populations, so the cleartext user-id must not be folded into the credential span and its own status stays open. The encoded token is the credential span.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for the cleartext user-id, and the extent of the encoded token is not asserted here either, so this fixture is a candidate only. The standard separates the identity effect of individual credentials from confidentiality of their content, but does not say the user-id is public. Needs a maintainer decision on user-id status and on how credential and PII populations are kept separate.

sources.supports: the exchange of those credentials will have the effect of identifying that user even if the content within credentials remains confidential

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
